frontmatter.title: MFCSC: a public FC–SC example
frontmatter.description: A tutorial for using MFCSC to integrate connectomes from different modalities

children.value: By the end of this tutorial you will be able to:
Download paired functional and structural connectomes.
Run MFCSC on the public 50-participant example.
Check its outputs against the published reference and view a mismatch matrix.
Exclude undefined scores when comparing connections across participants.
MFCSC estimates mismatch between functional connectivity (FC) and structural connectivity (SC). This walkthrough uses the
, then opens the actual results in a local browser report. The compiled Neurodesk tool runs without a MATLAB licence.

. This small companion script checks the example’s file pairing and matrix dimensions, reports invalid values, and creates a report for viewing. It uses NumPy and Matplotlib from the Neurodesk base Python environment.

children.value: Open the generated report from this terminal:

children.alt: The actual mismatch matrix and quality checks opened in Neurodesk Firefox

children.value: The report displays the first participant’s matrix using the common valid mask. Grey cells are excluded. The colour scale distinguishes positive and negative mismatch around zero. This run uses the tool’s default upper-triangle, within-hemisphere output, so the lower triangle and between-hemisphere blocks are grey. Region indices follow the supplied region-label file.
The common mask is a conservative choice for comparing the same connections across participants. It excludes undefined scores; it does not recover a score for a missing connection.

The same four-argument workflow can be used with appropriately prepared MEG and diffusion connectomes. Put the functional matrices in a separate folder, pair each with its corresponding structural matrix in a tab-separated list, and retain identical region definitions and ordering across both modalities. When using MFCSC, authors should cite:

Civier O, Sourty M, Calamante F (2023) MFCSC: Novel method to calculate mismatch between functional and structural brain connectomes, and its application for detecting hemispheric functional specialisations. Scientific Reports

Rubinov M, Sporns O (2010) Complex network measures of brain
connectivity: Uses and interpretations. NeuroImage 52:1059-69.
When using the structural connectivity matrices from OSF, authors should cite:

Civier O, Smith RE, Yeh CH, Connelly A, Calamante F (2019) Is removal of weak connections necessary for graph-theoretical analysis of dense weighted structural connectomes from diffusion MRI? NeuroImage
